**My reasoning:**

I have farmed this land in Quzhou for over 50 years. The North China Plain gives me one choice that makes sense above all others: the winter wheat and summer maize rotation. I have done this my whole life. The soil knows it, the market supports it, and the local agricultural station provides the seeds and technical guidance for exactly this system. I am not going to experiment at 70.

My children have moved to Shijiazhuang, so I am managing about 8 mu myself — I leased out the rest two years ago when my back worsened. Eight mu I can still handle with hired mechanization for tillage and harvest.

For wheat, I use the Jimai series — improved varieties, not hybrid. Wheat in this region is not hybrid. I apply base fertilizer before plowing, then top-dress nitrogen at the jointing stage. I irrigate at sowing, at overwintering, and again at heading — three times. I will spray once for weeds in autumn, once for powdery mildew and rust in spring, and once more pre-harvest if aphids appear.

For maize, I plant hybrid seed immediately after wheat harvest — no-tillage, directly into the stubble. Hybrid maize is standard here now; I stopped saving seed twenty years ago. I apply all phosphorus and potassium as base, split the nitrogen between base and big bell stage. Summer rain usually helps but I irrigate twice to be safe.

I expect about 450 kg/mu of wheat and 580 kg/mu of maize. These are reliable numbers for my land. I am not chasing record yields anymore. I want stable income and manageable labor.

Fertilizer rates reflect mature local practice: split nitrogen application for wheat at base and jointing, and for maize at base and big bell stage, with phosphorus and potassium applied as base fertilizer. I irrigate wheat three times (sowing, overwintering, heading) and maize twice given summer rainfall supplementation. Pesticide applications cover autumn herbicide and spring fungicide/insecticide for wheat, and herbicide plus corn borer control for maize. I use rotary tillage after maize harvest to prepare for wheat, and no-tillage direct seeding for maize after wheat harvest to save labor and moisture. My yield targets of 450 kg/mu wheat and 580 kg/mu maize reflect reliable, conservative expectations suited to my age, physical capacity, and preference for stable over speculative returns."
